cards.text: Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church in Corinth, and he's right in the middle of a brag. Not a little brag, friend. A FULL brag, and he says he must go on boasting, even though there's nothing to gain.

cards.question: Paul says there's nothing to gain, but he keeps boasting anyway. What does he move on to?

answers.text: Visions and revelations from the Lord
Praise he got from the other churches
His years of training as a Pharisee

cards.text: Paul says he knows a man in Christ who was caught up to the third heaven. FOURTEEN years ago. Friend, I can't remember what I stamped this morning.

cards.question: Paul says he knows for sure whether the man was in his body when he was caught up to the third heaven.

cards.text: Paul circles back to it: in the body or out of it, he doesn't know, but God knows. And this man was caught up to Paradise.

cards.question: The man was caught up to Paradise. What does Paul say about the things he heard there?

answers.text: No one is permitted to tell them
Every church needs to hear them
He wrote them all down later

cards.question: Paul will boast about a man like that. But when it comes to himself, he'll boast only in his weaknesses.
Paul says that if he wanted to boast about himself, he would be a fool.

cards.text: But Paul holds back anyway. He doesn't want anyone giving him more credit than what they see in him or hear from him, or because of these surpassingly great revelations.

cards.question: After those surpassingly great revelations, Paul says he was given something. What was it?
Paul says the thorn in his flesh was given to keep him from becoming ___.
Paul calls the thorn in his flesh a messenger of Satan, sent to torment him.

cards.text: Notice Paul never says what the thorn is. Whatever it was, it tormented him, and friend, I get ONE crumb stuck in my mustache and start acting like I need a doctor.

cards.question: Paul pleads with the Lord to take the thorn away from him. How many times?

cards.text: THREE times! Me? I sat in the back of a junk drawer for years and didn't ask anybody for anything. Then the Lord answers Paul.

cards.question: Paul has pleaded three times for the thorn to go. What does the Lord say to him?

answers.text: My grace is sufficient for you
My hand will lift it from you

cards.question: The Lord tells Paul why His grace is enough: "My power is perfected in ___."
Now Paul says he'll boast all the more gladly in his weaknesses. Why?

answers.text: So the power of Christ may rest on him
So the Corinthians will pray for him
So the false apostles will stop bragging

cards.text: That's why, for the sake of Christ, Paul delights in weaknesses, insults, hardships, persecutions and difficulties. DELIGHTS! Friend, I can't even delight in a burnt batch.

cards.question: Paul sums it all up: "For when I am weak, then I am ___."

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 17 quotes "My power is perfected in ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 20 quotes "For when I am weak, then I am ___.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The passage starts mid-thought, with Paul already boasting. The opening card says he is 'right in the middle of a brag' but never says why he is boasting. Chapter 11 gives the reason: he is answering the false apostles and boasting 'as a fool.' Without that, a baker hears an apostle bragging for no reason. That clashes with the passage's point about boasting in weakness.

rule.text: If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The card says Paul, an apostle, is writing to the church in Corinth. That fact comes from outside the passage (2 Corinthians 1:1), but the card cites only 2 Corinthians 12:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Paul says he knows...', 'FOURTEEN years ago.' and 'Friend, I can't remember...'. Only the opening card may go past two.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No story card sets up verse 6 before this true or false. The card right before it (card 7) says Paul will boast only in his weaknesses, which points the baker toward 'True.' The answer is 'False.' A baker can't reason this out, so it plays as a trick rather than an informed guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'THREE times!', 'Me?', 'I sat in the back...' and 'Then the Lord answers Paul.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke compares pleading with the Lord to Papa Dorin not asking anybody for anything, which is the opposite action. The comparison also frames Paul's three pleas as excessive next to Papa Dorin, so it laughs at Paul rather than with his situation.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'That's why...', 'DELIGHTS!' and 'Friend, I can't even delight in a burnt batch.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
